the rate of nitrate (NO₃-N) leaching is strongly influenced by the rate of N fertilizer input and the degree of influence depends on soil type, weather and cropping system.

the rate of NO 3 −N leaching increased at a N fertilizer rate greater than the N rate required to optimize the leachate load per kg grain in both continuous maize and the two-year maize–soybean rotation.

(i) there is a strong link, but not a linear one, between NO3-N leached from fertilized maize and the rate of N fertilizer input; (ii) the rate of NO2-N leaching increases sharply when the rate of N input increases beyond the agronomic optimum N input; (iii) the rate of increase of NO3-N is greater in continuous maize than in the maize-soya rotation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of nitrate-N leaching is a function of the N fertilizer rate, the crop type and rotation, the site, and the year.

the rate of NO 3 -N leaching is strongly related to the rate of N fertilizer application, and that rotating maize with soybean reduces the risk of overfertilizing and the associated NO3-N leachate load.
rotating maize reduces the risk of NO3-N loss and allows for a greater N fertilizer input before leaching increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leaching response to N fertilizer input is highly variable and depends on both cropping system and soil type.

the leaching-fertility response is highly dependent on the soil and cropping system, and that the rate of NO 3-N leaching is highly sensitive to N fertilizer rate, especially in continuous annual cropping systems.
